instructor.title: Starting as an Instructor
instructor.description: I started as an instructor at Alpha Tech, teaching Delphi programming, hardware, website design and basic computing. Five years of classes, corporate training and private lessons, and that's where I learned to explain what I knew.

transition.title: Transition to Development
transition.description: I left the classroom for software development, at Softpar. I worked on enterprise systems with Delphi and databases, and that's where I came to understand complex business rules and critical systems.

financial.title: 11 Years in Financial Systems
financial.description: My longest stint, at View Financial Systems: financial systems for checking accounts, documents and leasing. Almost everything was Delphi 7, until the client asked for digital signing of bank slips (boletos) and SOAP web services with digital certificates. Delphi couldn't handle it, and there were no components or budget to buy any. I proposed C#, a language I already knew well: I wrote a document with pros and cons, built an MVP of a .NET library exposed as COM+ on Windows, and had Delphi call the C# code through that interface. I presented it to the directors, they liked it, and it shipped.

modernization.title: Modernization and New Technologies
modernization.description: At Zylix, I worked on industrial automation and moved a .NET Framework and Windows Forms project to the web. Containerization, better security and client access to the software's features came with it. It was the step that took me fully into software architecture.

architect.title: Software Architect at Consilux
architect.description: I was hired at Consilux as a software architecture and development specialist, and started out giving internal consulting to several teams. Later I was handed part of a ride-hailing app system, Uber-style, split across three teams: the app and driver matching, financial control, and the company's own bank, which already had the white-label logic. I led the financial control team (the ledger, driver payments, and passenger and driver balances) as architect and developer, and we delivered solid work. When the CTO of CSX, a Consilux division, left, I took over the development team and the technology decisions, which is now my main job. I still support the whole company, and I'm currently working on vehicle radar systems and a digital wall. Among other cases, I rebuilt a file importer that took at least 3 days to import 1 day of files: after an architecture analysis and a new implementation, it takes under 1 hour.
